Now I see the issue. When `opt_error` is called (via longjmp), it jumps back to `bpf_optimize` which calls `opt_cleanup`. But `opt_init` already frees some of the pointers before calling `opt_error`. The problem is that when `opt_error` is called from within `opt_init` after some allocations have been freed and set to NULL, the `opt_cleanup` will try to free them again.

Wait, let me re-read. `opt_error` does a longjmp back to `bpf_optimize`, which then calls `opt_cleanup`. But `opt_init` already freed some pointers before calling `opt_error`. After the longjmp, those pointers are dangling (freed but not set to NULL), and `opt_cleanup` will free them again → double-free.
